metadata.dataset_name: Carbon Emission Factors Knowledge Base - India
metadata.purpose: Versioned JSON reference dataset for a carbon-emissions calculator. Load into application memory/cache; no model training is required.
metadata.geographic_focus: India where India-specific factors are available
metadata.calculation_principle: The backend performs deterministic calculations. Groq may interpret questions and explain results, but must not invent factors or calculate official results from memory.

important_terms.CO2e: Carbon dioxide equivalent, including other greenhouse gases converted using a stated global-warming-potential basis.
important_terms.activity_data: Measured quantity such as kWh electricity, litres of fuel, or kg of material/waste.
important_terms.emission_factor: Emissions per unit of activity, with a defined gas, boundary, geography, year, and source.

factor_status_definitions.verified_historical: The stated value and definition are supported by the cited source for the specified historical period.
factor_status_definitions.source_supported_boundary_review: A source supports the number, but its scope/boundary must be checked before use for the application's purpose.
factor_status_definitions.user_provided_unverified: Supplied by the project team; source and/or boundary not independently verified.
factor_status_definitions.not_for_production: Included for traceability only. Do not use as a default calculation factor until verified.
factor_status_definitions.scenario_not_inventory_factor: A future scenario value, not an observed factor for historical reporting.

sources.publisher: Central Electricity Authority, Government of India
sources.title: CO2 Baseline Database User Guide, Version 19.0
supports: 2022-23 Indian grid weighted-average emission rate including cross-border electricity transfers: 0.823 tCO2/MWh
2022-23 weighted-average emission rate including RES and cross-border transfers: 0.716 tCO2/MWh
sources.limitations: These are different metrics. The factor must be chosen to match the reporting purpose and method. Do not treat operating margin as the same as the grid-average factor.

sources.publisher: Central Electricity Authority, Government of India
sources.title: CDM - CO2 Baseline Database portal
supports: Current portal lists Baseline Carbon Dioxide Emission Database Version 22.0 and earlier versions
sources.limitations: For a live production deployment, retrieve the selected version's workbook/user guide and record exact table, metric, and reference year.

sources.title: Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero - Sectoral Insights: Industry (Vol. 4)
supports: Annexure II process factors for clinker, prebaked aluminium, soda ash, and route-specific ethylene
Annexure III projected grid emission factors for 2025, 2050, and 2070 scenarios
sources.limitations: The report states it is an analytical study, not a policy statement. Annexure II values are industrial-process and product-use (IPPU) factors, not automatically full lifecycle footprints. Annexure III future values are scenario projections, not observed historical factors.

sources.title: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
supports: Inventory methodologies for fuel combustion and waste categories
sources.limitations: Methodological guidance is not itself a verified India-specific per-litre petrol/diesel or generic kg-waste factor. Exact volume-to-energy conversions require fuel properties and a defined method.

sources.publisher: Government of India submitted to UNFCCC
sources.title: India National Inventory Report 2024
supports: National inventory methods and category-specific estimates
sources.limitations: A national inventory table must be matched to the exact fuel, gas, category, and unit before deriving an application factor.

formulas.name: Activity data multiplied by emission factor

formulas.note: Example is for historical demonstration only; select the factor appropriate to the report year and methodology.

formulas.name: Convert factor from tonnes CO2 per tonne material to kg CO2 per kg material
formulas.note: Numerically equal because both numerator and denominator are multiplied by 1000. Confirm both units refer to the same product and boundary.

formulas.name: Direct fuel combustion
formulas.note: Only use a factor explicitly defined per litre for the specific fuel and direct-combustion boundary. This is not automatically well-to-wheel or lifecycle emissions.

formulas.name: Waste treatment emissions
formulas.output_unit: kg CO2 or kg CO2e according to factor
formulas.note: The factor must match composition, treatment route, geography, methane capture, time horizon, and gas-accounting basis.

research_findings.finding: CEA Version 19.0 reports for FY 2022-23, including cross-border transfers, a weighted-average rate of 0.823 tCO2/MWh, a weighted-average rate including RES of 0.716 tCO2/MWh, and simple operating margin of 0.971 tCO2/MWh.
research_findings.impact: These are not interchangeable. The project's original 0.716 value is supported only when the RES-inclusive metric is intended.

research_findings.finding: As checked on 2026-10-09, CEA's official portal lists Version 22.0 as the newest listed baseline database.
research_findings.impact: For current reporting, inspect Version 22.0 workbook and select the matching metric. Keep historical factors available for historical years.

research_findings.finding: NITI Aayog 2026 Annexure II gives 0.5292 tCO2 per tonne of clinker produced. Clinker is not the same product as finished cement.
research_findings.impact: Keep the supplied cement value 0.76 as unverified and do not replace it with the clinker factor unless the activity is specifically clinker production.

research_findings.finding: NITI Aayog 2026 lists a prebaked-technology process factor of 1.6 tCO2 per tonne of aluminium, and separately lists CF4 and C2F6 quantities.
research_findings.impact: This process-only CO2 value is not directly comparable to the supplied 26 kg CO2/kg aluminium value without checking the lifecycle boundary and whether non-CO2 gases are included.

research_findings.finding: NITI Aayog 2026 gives route-specific ethylene process factors of 1.73 tCO2/t via naphtha and 0.76 tCO2/t via ethane. It distinguishes soda ash industry intensity (1.28 tCO2/t) from process-only IPPU factor (0.323 tCO2/t).
research_findings.impact: Store each factor as a separate record with its route and boundary. Do not average duplicates or choose a factor without knowing the production route and purpose.

research_findings.finding: The supplied petrol 2.371 kg CO2/L and diesel 2.64 kg CO2/L were not matched here to an exact official source table that establishes the stated unit and boundary.
research_findings.impact: Retain for traceability, but disable them for default calculations until the exact source, fuel specification, and direct-combustion versus lifecycle boundary are verified.

research_findings.finding: Waste factors depend on waste composition, treatment route, methane capture, and whether the output is CO2 or CO2e. A generic factor of 0.3 cannot be assumed valid for all waste and scrap types.
research_findings.impact: Keep generic waste factor inactive and add separate factors only when source and treatment method are documented.

research_findings.finding: The project asked for data up to the last three years. The dataset includes historical data for 2022-23 where verified and separately records a 2025 NITI scenario value. The 2026 NITI industry report is a newer technical source but its process factors should not be mislabelled as 2022-23 factors.
research_findings.impact: Reference year describes the factor's actual data/method period, not the publication date. Never backdate a 2026 source factor to 2022-23 unless the source explicitly supports that period.

runtime_recommendations.json_file_role: Versioned source dataset and local seed file
runtime_recommendations.fastapi: Load and validate this JSON once during application startup; expose lookup methods by factor_id/category/year/boundary. Do not reread the file on every request unless hot reload is intended.
runtime_recommendations.postgresql: Later, normalize factors, sources, factor versions, and audit changes into tables. Keep the JSON as a reproducible import/export artifact.
runtime_recommendations.groq: Use the model for natural-language input parsing and explanation. Have backend code choose the factor and calculate results. Include the factor source, year, boundary, and status in the response.
before_public_launch: Verify all user_provided_unverified and not_for_production entries against exact source tables.
Decide whether the app reports direct CO2 or CO2e.
Define whether material factors are process-only, cradle-to-gate, or full lifecycle.
For electricity, select the exact CEA metric and reporting year.
For waste, specify composition and treatment method.
Add unit tests for conversions and known examples.
Log factor_id and dataset version with every calculation for auditability.
